LIFE RIGHTS DECEPTION

By: Graham Coetzer | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Two years after we first exposed how two brothers at the head of a property development scheme worth billions were taking advantage of their elderly customers, we return to find that dozens of victims

Unique Selling Point:
Brothers Willem and Billy Steyn own the Belvedere Group of Retirement Villages. After our last story they seem to have rebranded as Retirewell SA on their website. They sell life rights to elderly people wanting to move into one of their 12 retirement estates. On paper, the offer is good. In return for paying anything from about R1million - R2.5 million for a unit in one of the estates, you own the life rights to live in the unit until you pass away or want to move out. Once that happens, Belvedere will sell your unit on your behalf, and you will get your initial capital back minus a commision fee and any profit Belvedere makes on the sale. But that is not happening - leaving bereaved family members to deal with the double blow of losing a loved one and not being able to wind up their estates or receive the money owed to them.

Summary:
Last time around the Steyn brothers agreed to an interview with us and said that Covid was having a huge effect on their business and that they would and wanted to pay everyone back. While we only had a handful of complaints during our first story, the list has now grown to 35 cases where people have not been paid out. That's despite the fact that in at least 7 of those the complainants have received court orders compelling Belvedere to pay them the monies owed. The litigation has cost some case studies R500 000 to receive R1million owed, and taken years to complete. But Belvedere are using the courts and their lawyers
to stall, and many case studies simply don't have the money to take them to court. Worst of all, Belvedere are ignoring the court orders, leaving our case studies at their wits end.

Further information:
We have done a hidden camera investigation to see if Belvedere were using the same promises when selling the units.
I have asked the City Of Johannesburg to supply us with the results of an investigation that they started in November 2022 regarding the legalities of the retirement villages in regards to their zoning, town planning etc paper work.
I have asked the Legal Practice Council to respond to allegations that the Steyn's attorney, Juliana Steyn, has been reported to LPC on several occasions and to provide me with feedback on the cases.
I have followed up with our previous case studies.

Script:


Life Rights Deception | Third Draft Script | 07 November 2023

PREAMBLE….teaser opening/context  

Voice: 
On Johannesbrug’s West Rand: row upon row of retirement estates, built on the promise of a carefree lifestyle… and a well-deserved rest. 

Ups their video 
Willem: We really love to create the best environment…

Voice
Marketed to people over 50, the developments offer landscaped complexes, centered around community hubs, with all the amenities: libraries, exercise classes, bingo, and above all security. 

Ups their video 
Billy: We really love to be involved, as well as our children. Everybody in the family is involved in this business. And we take it very seriously.

Voice
It promises not just a good life but, critically, a secure investment in the form of a life right. 

Ups their video 
Willem: So we are really sitting with a community of happy people

Ups Covid footage
Social distancing, put on your masks!

Voice
But as the Covid-19 lockdown struck two years ago, we investigated a disturbing trend of families left high and dry when it came to cashing in their investment in the Belvedere Group. 

And in the years since our story, there have been some startling developments - and now even greater injustices.

Sound Up Richard Boys: 
What’s next for the problem over here? I believe this is an absolute crisis.
DIP TO BLACK OPENING SEQUENCE OVER

Act 1 - Recap 
Sound Up Covid 19 News:  
“The lockdown in South Africa was imposed suddenly” | “Data shows how deep Covid-19 has rocked South Africa’s economy”

Voice: 
It was 2021. Lianne Silver, grappling with level-three lockdown and mourning her mother Shirley's death for a year … faced the challenge of trying to get a refund out of Belvedere's Harveston Retirement Village, where her mother had invested over R700,000.

Sound Up Lianne Silver: 
It was meant to be that I wouldn’t have to wait when she had died…And in the contract itself, it said 30 days she would be paid out, and so it sounded wonderful and rosy.

Voice: 
Life Rights ownership sounds appealing: there’s the security of a lifestyle village…for life. Should you move on or pass away, the developers resell your property and refund the initial investment.

But even a year after Lianne’s mother’s unit was sold, they were still owed R715 000 - money her mother had earmarked for other uses.

Sound Up Lianne: 
But mostly for my adopted niece and nephew, Kayla and Joshua.

They have stolen her whole life’s work. It’s a disgrace, it really is a disgrace.

Voice:
When we confronted the men behind the Belvedere Group back in 2021, they invited us to a crowded hall, having commandeered some residents to bolster their PR.  

Property developer brothers Willem and Billy Steyn confirmed they were trustees on virtually all the trusts that own R2.4 billion worth of Belvedere retirement villages.

Sound Up Willem Steyn:
I am basically I would say on at least half of them, and Billy is probably on the other half, more or less.

Voice:
Why hadn’t they paid out the distraught families whose stories we’d brought to them? Their answer at the time… Covid, of course. 

Sound Up Billy Steyn
We’re still struggling to get funds in in terms of normal operation. From last year with Covid, lockdowns with the council, lockdowns with the deeds office etc.

Voice:
But their answers did little to soothe distressed families in financial need.

Sound Up Willem Steyn
I’m not rich, I am wealthy. Stinking wealthy.

ACT 2 …the feedback after the last story & new undercover

Link Masa
It’s been two and a half years since we first met the Steyn brothers, and according to some residents of their retirement villages, things have gotten worse.

Voice:
Joburg Attorney Reon Marais was representing Liane Silver when we interviewed her last time.

Sound Up Reon
Masa: What's happened since then?

Reon: in consequence of the airing of the Carte Blanche program on the last occasion, it was a short while after that I ….checked my trust account and saw that there was money paid into the trust account. So the Steyn brothers had then paid the capital amount and in fact, I think they added some interest to it as well.

Masa: That’s surprising even to us.

Reon: The other result of that airing is that I’ve had many more people with the same problem contact me. 

Voice:
He wasn’t the only one - the civil rights organisation Afriforum, as well as our viewer submission inbox - saw a steady drip feed of Belvedere-related complaints.

Soon the Steyns turned filmmakers, releasing “The truth about Belvedere Villages” that claimed our complainants were less than three per cent of their business.

Link Masa
Billy Youtube: 97, 98% of the people living here in terms of normal operations, they’re happy. 
Masa: While they claim that this is only two to three percent of their business, it’s actually two to three percent too many. 

Voice
we now have 34 new cases where Belvedere have sold units, and not paid out the capital.

Link Masa completes
Masa:  That’s 34 families that have been left in financial and emotional distress.

Voice
Heather Boys’s husband Colin is in frail care after several brain surgeries - they needed to move out of their Belvedere unit.

Sound Up Heather
Because he’s had for the last number of years, he’s had health issues.

Voice
Their son Richard took up their battle.

Sound Up Richard
Richard: From September 2020, the new Life rights owner had paid the full sum stipulated in the contract to purchase their life right on the unit.
Masa: And did they then pay your parents after the 30-day period like they had promised?
Richard: No. So the clock really started ticking in October 2020.
Voice:
The delay is making it hard for them to meet Colin's medical expenses. They went to court within a year - where Belvedere played legal cat-and-mouse games..withholding documents, delaying dates… settling at the very last legal moment when nerves are frayed..  


Sound Up Richard
Richard: That out-of-court settlement agreement becomes an order of the court.

Masa: Did they stick to it?

Richard: No. They paid on the 1st of March 2023, quite according to the contract, and they have defaulted on the other five out of six instalments since March 2023.

Masa:  What kind of toll is this taking on your parents?
Richard: I think the dignity of an old person when these contracts are not honoured. It takes a toll on them.
Voice
As things stand, the Steyn brothers owe Heather and Colin over a million rand.

In the meantime, they’ve rebranded their service offering as “RetirewellSA”. 

We wondered - if their failure to pay out, in contempt of court, is so rife.. Do they warn new buyers what they’re letting themselves in for?

Sound Up Hidden Camera
Woman: Okay then it’s got two bedrooms?

Agent: No three bedrooms

Woman: Three bedrooms?

Agent: pièce de résistance!

Voice
We sent in an undercover couple to film the marketing tour …

Sound Up Hidden camera
Agent: We have this over here which is rather nice.

Voice
and then the long-time agent gets down to the lowdown on life rights.

Sound Up Hidden camera
Agent: …what you pay less commission is what you get back…Because what you’re buying here, is not a place, a house. It’s a lifestyle that’s completely conducive to retirement.

Voice:
So conducive, that many people will be queueing up, if you ever want to sell.

Sound Up Hidden Camera
We sell the house, it normally gets paid out after 30 days, with an estate it might take a bit longer, but it’s not a long time, these houses sell, because they’re good.

Voice:
So no warning at all to prospective buyers. 
And what if you don’t have a lawyer on call?

Link Masa
There seems to be a pattern. The only way to get your money or even just a portion of it is to go through the courts. But have the Steyn brothers found a loophole that helps them get off the hook by dragging the case?

Voice
Reon Marais believes the Belvedere brothers may well be taking advantage of people’s ignorance when it comes to understanding debt – whereby they only have three years to legally challenge the brothers to repay the amount due.
Sound Up Reon Marais
Masa: So wait, does that mean that the Steyn brothers can get away with not paying these brothers after three years?
Reon: If they stall them long enough…then that’s the end of that claim. The Steyn brothers, or the Belvedere Group, or whoever it is involved say yes we will pay you, well when are you going to pay?
ACT 3 … ROR & theft charge 

Voice:
This is exactly what Ingrid Lotze is asking - having waited for seven years by now. After her mother Violet died in 2016, her family have received only one-third of the money they’re due.

Sound Up Ingrid
Ingrid: And we’re sitting after demands, and summonses, and going to the high court, and changing attorneys, and going to the ombudsman…

Voice:
In 2018 the high court ordered that Ingrid be paid out R1.1 million owed to her mom’s estate in three equal tranches.

Sound Up Ingrid
And we really had to continue to fight until we got that first tranche. And that is where it ended.

Voice:
and going back to court has become too daunting.

Sound Up Ingrid
Is anybody sane going to spend R500 000 to get that from Belvedere Estate? And they know that.

Voice:
We reached out to the brothers again.

Sound Up Willem Steyn
Masa: Mr Steyn, I’m just checking because we wanted to do an on-camera interview with you but I’ve been told that you’ve opted for a written response, did you receive the email with our questions?

Willem: Yes I did receive that and we decided to go for a no reply on that one.

Masa: Why is that?

Willem: Because I’ve done a comprehensive interview with Derek Watts.

Masa: …we have more complaints then we did the last time? So we’d like to get some answers, why are you continuing with this?

Willem: You can just listen to the interview that we had with him, that was as comprehensive as it can be.

Masa: But the question still remains why you aren’t paying these people when you’ve received the money?

Willem: That is a no reply from us thank you so much. 

Masa: And he has hung up. He thinks the information from an interview done two and a half years ago is sufficient.

Sound Up Richard Boys
I believe we are sitting here with a very vulnerable group of people in society, and a lot of them are scared to put their heads out over the trenches because they are frankly intimidated by the Steyn brothers

Voice: 
Reon Marais says one of his clients has now resorted to opening a criminal case.



Sound Up Reon
Because in our view the court will find that this is a situation of theft…

Sound Up Heather
Masa: If the Steyn brothers were to walk in right now, what would you say to them?

Heather: Shall I tell you? Voetsek!

Sound Up Richard
The shouldn’t have to fight things like this. They shouldn't have to fight this. It’s not golden years, it’s stolen years that we’re dealing with here.
ENDS
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PROMO1
 
VO
Distraught family members, and property assets worth billions, three years after our first story about questionable retirement home developers aired, they’re still at it.
 
Upsound
Masa: A lot has changed, more people have come out to complain, we have more complaints then we did the last time?.
 
VO
Is enough being done to protect the elderly and vulnerable?
 
 
 
 
PROMO2
VO
Once their retirement homes were sold, they were supposed to be paid out relatively quickly - or so they thought.
 
Upsound Richard Boys
What’s next for the problem over here? I believe this is an absolute crisis.
 
VO
We investigate property developers accused of reneging on promises to the elderly.
 
Upsound Phone engaged
 Masa: You have so much to answer to…
 
 
PROMO3
VO
They’re worth billions after they sold life rights to their elderly customers.
 
Upsound Ingrid
“So we’re sitting six years later. And we’re sitting after demands, and summonses, and going to the high court.
 
VO
Why are some family members having to fight for years in court to get their loved ones money back?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Two years after we first exposed how two brothers at the head of a property development scheme worth billions were taking advantage of their elderly customers, we return to find that dozens of victims
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Brothers Willem and Billy Steyn own the Belvedere Group of Retirement Villages. After our last story they seem to have rebranded as Retirewell SA on their website. They sell life rights to elderly people wanting to move into one of their 12 retirement estates. On paper, the offer is good. In return for paying anything from about R1million - R2.5 million for a unit in one of the estates, you own the life rights to live in the unit until you pass away or want to move out. Once that happens, Belvedere will sell your unit on your behalf, and you will get your initial capital back minus a commision fee and any profit Belvedere makes on the sale. But that is not happening - leaving bereaved family members to deal with the double blow of losing a loved one and not being able to wind up their estates or receive the money owed to them.
metadata.Summary: Last time around the Steyn brothers agreed to an interview with us and said that Covid was having a huge effect on their business and that they would and wanted to pay everyone back. While we only had a handful of complaints during our first story, the list has now grown to 35 cases where people have not been paid out. That's despite the fact that in at least 7 of those the complainants have received court orders compelling Belvedere to pay them the monies owed. The litigation has cost some case studies R500 000 to receive R1million owed, and taken years to complete. But Belvedere are using the courts and their lawyers to stall, and many case studies simply don't have the money to take them to court. Worst of all, Belvedere are ignoring the court orders, leaving our case studies at their wits end.
metadata.Further information: We have done a hidden camera investigation to see if Belvedere were using the same promises when selling the units. I have asked the City Of Johannesburg to supply us with the results of an investigation that they started in November 2022 regarding the legalities of the retirement villages in regards to their zoning, town planning etc paper work. I have asked the Legal Practice Council to respond to allegations that the Steyn's attorney, Juliana Steyn, has been reported to LPC on several occasions and to provide me with feedback on the cases. I have followed up with our previous case studies.
metadata.Reason for hidden camera: To film sales pitch and confirm if they are still making same promises
metadata.Reason for legal: Allegations against the Steyn brothers and their attorney
